title: Options: calls, puts and payoffs
objectives: Define call and put and compute buyer and seller payoffs.
body_md:
An **option** gives the buyer a **right** (not an obligation) to buy or sell at the **strike price**, in exchange for a **premium**.

| Position | Right / obligation | Max loss | Max gain |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Long call** | Right to buy | Premium | Unlimited |
| **Short call** | Obligation to sell | Unlimited | Premium |
| **Long put** | Right to sell | Premium | Strike − premium (price to zero) |
| **Short put** | Obligation to buy | Strike − premium | Premium |

## Payoffs at expiry (per unit)

- Long call = max(S − K, 0) − premium
- Long put = max(K − S, 0) − premium
- **Breakeven**: call = K + premium; put = K − premium

## Style

**European** options exercise only at expiry; **American** any time. Index options in India are European; stock options in India are European as well (verify).

Example: call K = 100, premium 5, spot 112 at expiry: profit = 12 − 5 = **7**; breakeven 105.

> **Exam tip:** Buyer's loss is capped at premium; the seller's isn't.
example: Long put K = 500, premium 15. At expiry spot = 460: payoff 40 − 15 = 25 profit. At spot 520: lose the 15 premium.
say: As a buyer your maximum loss is the premium paid.
A seller can lose far more than the premium received.
never: Option buyers can lose more than the premium.
Selling an option has limited risk.
